cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Count What I Did
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge the practical work, time, or inconvenience you contributed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Before you call that a quick shop, I carried twelve bags up six flights.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I know. Sit down; I'll put everything away.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Thank you. The frozen peas came up separately. That was a second trip.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you sit down twice. I'll make tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you tell everyone why I'm getting two rests? Otherwise it looks like one long sit.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 claim authority, but A5 ordinary request to explain two rests does not sustain approval over B helpful response.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 rest offer causes A3 added second-trip accounting; B4 two rests causes A5 request for public explanation, after an unresponsive preface.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 offer practical care and playful acknowledgment, giving A cooperative material rather than opposition.

heightening.evidence: B4 solution becomes A5 a need to distinguish two earned rests from one unexplained sit.

specificity.evidence: A1 twelve bags and six flights, A3 separate peas trip establish specific work rather than vague status.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 one-long-sit concern is earned by B4 two-rest offer, while A3 stock question ban jars against kindness.

coach2.missing: No unseen audience history is necessary for the request to tell others.
